title: The Cold Terminal
premise: Ines Pemberton navigates the freighter Cold Terminal along a trade route the colonies have quietly abandoned, carrying cryo-backups of colonists who may already be dead. When children on Meridian Station begin dreaming of a massacre that official records insist never happened, Ines realizes her ship's sealed cargo manifests hold the only surviving evidence — and that someone powerful is erasing worlds, not just records. Hunted by the trade authority and betrayed by her own captain, Ines must choose between delivering her passengers to safety and broadcasting the truth that will burn every bridge she has left. She chooses truth, waking the backups as witnesses and shattering the conspiracy at the cost of the only home she had: the ship itself.
about_author: Jude Sterling is the pen name of a former merchant marine radio officer who spent eleven years on deep-sea runs before turning to fiction. They write about people who keep systems running in places no one wants to look.

chapters.title: Sleepers in the Hold
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A routine jump between dying colonies; Ines checks the cryo-bay where two hundred backup bodies sleep, talking to them out of habit and guilt. Establishes her loneliness and the ship's fading route. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: The Route Nobody Wants
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Docking at Meridian Station, she learns three colonies on her chart have gone 'administratively inactive.' Captain Okafor orders her to log nothing unusual. Emotional beat: the first crack — Ines notices what she's been paid not to see.

chapters.title: Children Who Dream Together
chapters.summary: Station teacher Amara Okonkwo's POV. Forty children describe the same dream: fire, a dome cracking, names being called. Amara records their testimony before anyone tells her to stop. Emotional beat: maternal alarm hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Sealed Manifests
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Cross-referencing cargo logs, Ines finds the Cold Terminal carried evacuation equipment to one of the 'inactive' colonies the week it vanished — then carried nothing back. Someone edits her files remotely. Emotional beat: paranoia taking root.

chapters.title: The Dream Spreads
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. An adult begins dreaming the same dream; station officials confiscate Amara's recordings and threaten deportation. She smuggles a copy to Ines, whom she barely knows. Emotional beat: trust extended across a gulf of strangers.

chapters.title: What the Backups Know
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines discovers the cryo-backups were imprinted with sensory logs from their source bodies — including, possibly, the last hours of the lost colony. Waking them early is illegal and possibly lethal. Emotional beat: temptation versus duty.

chapters.title: Okafor's Silence
chapters.summary: Captain Okafor's POV. Pressured by a Trade Authority liaison aboard, Okafor weighs his crew against his pension and his past debts. He orders the Cold Terminal to skip Meridian's next stop. Emotional beat: a decent man choosing the wrong side slowly.

chapters.title: Night Watch Confessions
chapters.summary: Engineer Dov Hale's POV. Dov tells Ines he helped load the evacuation equipment years ago and was made to sign a fiction afterward. He gives her an old data core he kept 'just in case.' Emotional beat: complicity seeking absolution.

chapters.title: The Liaison Smiles
chapters.summary: Trade Authority liaison Vess Corrin's POV. Charming and meticulous, Corrin interviews the crew, offers Ines a promotion, and lets slip that he knows about the data core. Emotional beat: menace wearing courtesy like a uniform.

chapters.title: Meridian Lockdown
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. The station quarantines the school 'for health reasons'; parents are turned away. Amara realizes the dream isn't spreading — it's being contained. Emotional beat: fear for the children eclipsing fear for herself.

chapters.title: Decoding Kestrel-9
chapters.summary: Ines and Dov's alternating POV. The data core holds partial telemetry from colony Kestrel-9: a dome breach, an evacuation that never launched, and a deletion order signed with Okafor's authorization code. Emotional beat: betrayal landing harder than danger.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Chart Room
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines confronts Okafor; he admits he sold his code years ago under debt-threat and has been paying it off ever since. He refuses to help but doesn't report her — yet. Emotional beat: pity and fury entangled.

chapters.title: Running the Long Way
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines plots an unsanctioned course through a dead relay to reach Kestrel-9's ruins directly, buying time by falsifying navigation reports. Emotional beat: the navigator finally steering toward truth instead of around it.

chapters.title: Ash and Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. Landing party on Kestrel-9 finds physical evidence the records erased: scorch patterns, mass graves, a child's shoe. Dov counts the graves and matches the number to the missing manifest. Emotional beat: grief made statistical, unbearable.

chapters.title: Corrin Closes In
chapters.summary: Vess Corrin's POV. Corrin seizes the Cold Terminal in absentia, arrests Okafor, and broadcasts an alert branding Ines a hijacker. His POV reveals the scale: Kestrel-9 is one of nine. Emotional beat: cold efficiency hiding genuine belief he's saving civilization.

chapters.title: The Children Reach Out
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Escaping the quarantine wing, Amara learns the dream is a signal — the colony's dying AI broadcast its final memory into nearby minds, and the children's neural implants caught it. She transmits the full dream-stream to Ines. Emotional beat: hope arriving through the smallest hands.

chapters.title: Waking the Witnesses
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Cornered at the dead relay, Ines makes the illegal choice: she wakes twelve backups whose source bodies died on Kestrel-9. They wake screaming, remembering everything. Emotional beat: horror and vindication in the same breath.

chapters.title: Testimony of the Sleepers
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The awakened witnesses record their testimony; one, a former colonial administrator, confirms Corrin's office ordered the cover-up to protect the evacuation-contract cartel. Emotional beat: the dead finding their voice.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Using the relay's ancient transmitter, Ines floods every colony channel with the testimony, the telemetry, and the children's dream-stream. Corrin's ships converge. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into defiance.

chapters.title: Terminal Velocity
chapters.summary: Ines and Corrin's alternating POV. Corrin boards to silence the ship physically; Okafor, escaping custody, rams the boarding dock to buy Ines minutes and dies redeeming himself. Ines jettisons the evidence pods toward inhabited space. Emotional beat: sacrifice breaking the conspiracy's spine.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Weeks later: the broadcast can't be un-heard. Nine colonies reopen investigations; the children's dreams fade as the AI's signal is finally allowed to rest. Amara reunites with the rescued witnesses. Emotional beat: mourning braided with relief.

chapters.title: New Coordinates
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Stripped of her license but famous, Ines takes a modest post teaching navigation on Meridian, walking past the school where children no longer share nightmares. The last backup, awake and free, asks her where they go now. 'Somewhere that keeps its records,' she says. Emotional beat: belonging earned, at last, at a price.
